نَضِيدٌ and ↓ مَنْضُودٌ (Msb, K,) and ↓ مُنَضَّدٌ , [or the last has an intensive signification, as is shewn above,] Goods, household-goods, or commodities, (K,) put one upon another: (Msb, K:) [or put, or set, together, in regular order, or piled up: and the last, put one upon another, or side by side, compactly: see 1]. ―
-b2- طَلْعٌ نَضِيدٌ, in the Kur, [l. 10.] Spadices of palm-trees [having their flowers] compacted, or compactly disposed; (L;) yet in their envelopes; (Fr, L;) for when they have come forth therefrom they cease to be نضيد. (L.) ―
-b3- ↓ طَلْحٌ مَنْضُودٌ , in the Kur, [lvi. 28,] Gum-acacias having fruit or leaves closely set, one above another, from bottom to top, without their trunks being apparent below. (L.) ―
-b4- شَجَرُ الخَنَّةِ نَضِيدٌ مِنْ أَصْلِهَا إِلَى فَرْعِهَا The trees of paradise are closely set with leaves and fruit, one above another, from bottom to top, without having trunks apparent: (L, from a trad.:) and similarly ↓ نَضُودٌ (Jel, lvi. 20.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
